newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore leaders win record libel damages.
newsitem.headline: Singapore leaders win record libel damages.

text.p: A Singapore court awarded Prime Minister Goh Chok Tong and senior colleagues in his ruling party a record Singapore $8.08 (US$5.65) million in damages on Thursday in their libel cases against a political foe.

In a written judgment, the court ordered Tang Liang Hong, who fled the country after losing in January general elections, to pay the damages to Goh and 10 other members of the ruling People's Action party (PAP) for calling them liars.
Goh, involved in three of the suits against Tang, was awarded S$1.4 million. Former prime minister Lee Kuan Yew, involved in five of the cases, won the biggest amount -- S$2.3 million.
The PAP leaders had demanded aggravated damages totalling S$12.9 million.
"This court must show its indignation at the injury inflicted on the plaintiffs," Justice Chao Hick Tin said in the judgment handed to reporters.
"It cannot be disputed that in terms of aggravation, these 13 cases have no equal," he said.
Tang, who lost the cases in March when he did not return to defend himself, told Reuters last week he intended to appeal against the damages award.
He was sued by the PAP leaders for calling them liars for branding him an "anti-Christian Chinese chauvinist" who endangered Singapore's ethnic harmony

Justice Chao made clear that he agreed to the requests of the PAP leaders for aggravated damages because Tang had continued to criticise them in media interviews after fleeing to the south Malaysian state of Johor.
"The more enormous, outrageous, scandalous or scurrilous the defamation, and/or aggravation, the greater the damages," he said.
He also hinted that there could be further action to come against Tang, who was heavily criticised by judges for his manoevering during a rash of court hearings leading up to the damages award.
"Whether Mr Tang should be dealt with for scandalising the courts is a matter which may have to be taken up at some other time," Chao said.
Tang also faces 33 tax evasion charges and last week a court ordered his arrest.

He was charged formally in court on Friday and faces a fine of three times the amount of tax he is accused of evading -- S$211,000 -- plus a fine of S$10,000 on each charge. He could also be jailed for three years on each charge.
